tests.asserted: The test needs the real worker. If pw-probe-runner is missing it throws TestFailure, so it fails instead of skipping. Setup: actor A has no policy applied (policy "", applies:false). In phase 0, A issues token 0, transfers it to itself (delivery 0, a_to_a) and to B (delivery 1, a_to_b). In phase 2, A consumes delivery 0. Actor B applies cPolicy. In phase 1, B consumes delivery 1 twice (b_first with handle 1 and lastUse:false, then b_again with handle 2) and releases handle 1 and handle 2. The authority plan names a_to_b as the token's lastUseSlot. The test asserts: (1) outcome.cancelled is nil. (2) There are exactly 3 visits and every endReason is "completed". (3) There are exactly 2 transfers, both acknowledged PWTransferAck.delivered, with recipientActorIndex [0,1] in that order. (4) When the scheduler callback fires with phase==1, B's inbound slot 0 acknowledgement (a load-acquire at slotAcknowledgedOffset) equals PWAuthorityAck.accepted and B's session completedSlotCount is 0. If the callback never fires for phase 1, both stay nil and the equality checks fail. (5) b_first and b_again are both completed, at a callBoundary, with unavailableCode 0. (6) Each release completed. Its unavailableCode must be 2 if the matching consume's nativeResult was -1, and 0 otherwise. (7) a_consume, which runs in a later visit after the token's last declared transfer, is completed at a callBoundary with unavailableCode 0. (8) outcome.custody has exactly one record and its erased flag is true. The force-unwraps (index[...]!, sessions[1]!, custody!, inbound(0)!, slot(...)!) crash the test if any value is missing.
tests.recorded_only: The test writes no report. Several values are read but never fixed to an expected value. The kernel results (nativeResult) of b_first, b_again and a_consume are used only to choose the expected release code, so a consume that returned -1 is accepted. Raw handle values are never compared, so the comment 'distinct lifecycle references even when the raw handles agree' is not checked. When custody was erased is never observed; only the final flag is checked. Nothing checks whether B's cPolicy was applied or what it did, whether the transfers carried equal token bytes, or what happened to the lastUse:false flag. The variable named bCompletedAtPhase0End is actually sampled inside the phase==1 callback. The code does not show exactly when that callback runs relative to the end of phase 0 or the start of B's work.
fails_on: pw-probe-runner is absent (workerPresent false), which throws TestFailure instead of skipping
the scheduler cancels the run, or any visit ends with a reason other than completed, or the visit count is not 3
the self-transfer (a_to_a) or the A-to-B transfer is not acknowledged delivered, there are not exactly 2 transfers, or the recipient indices are wrong or out of order
B's inbound slot is not acknowledged 'accepted' while B is parked, e.g. acceptance only happens lazily once B's visit starts
B has already completed one or more slots when the phase-1 callback fires, i.e. B consumed before its phase was released
the phase-1 callback is never invoked, leaving both sampled values nil
a consume (including the repeated b_again on the same delivery) is reported unavailable, not completed, or not at a call boundary

a release reports an unavailable code that does not match its own consume's result, e.g. the second release is reported unavailable because the two consumes were merged into one lifecycle reference, or a release reports 0 after a failed consume
A's phase-2 consume of its self-delivered token is unavailable or incomplete because custody erasure invalidated the delivery
custody is not marked erased at the end, or there is not exactly one custody record
a named slot, B's session, the custody regions or B's inbound slot 0 is missing (force-unwrap crash)
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'the kernel actually honoured the repeated consumes and A's self-delivered consume, granting access'. Not supported, because nativeResult is never asserted: a consume that returned -1 passes as long as its release reports code 2, and no file access is attempted under cPolicy. Also not supported: that custody was erased exactly at a_to_b (only the final erased flag is checked); that B never consumed before its release at any time (there is a single sample at the phase-1 callback); and that the raw handles agreed while the references stayed distinct (handles are never compared).

tests.asserted: This is a module-level Python script that uses plain asserts and has no test framework. It runs four kinds of check. (1) apparatus_complete, applied to every run (principal, calibration and each contrast). It asserts: the envelope passes consumer.validate and lifecycle_oracle.check_record with no errors; execution_form is 'actors'; worker_exit_witness reports true; the set of actor ids equals the spec's; every actor has a distinct launch pid. For each actor: equipment requested == resolved == the spec's request; requirements are satisfied; execution status is matched and eligible; the execution pid is the launch pid; the equipment binding has the requested role, source 'packaged' and implementation_identity 'inventory_verified'; the subprocess was reaped with exit code 0 under the same pid; parent_pid is the runner pid. Actors with a policy: mode apply, applied True, application_count 1, application {observed, applied_publication}, and policy_sha256 == sha256(expected source) == policy_received_sha256. Actors without one: mode unapplied, application_count 0, {not_requested, unapplied_declaration}. Every phase shows arrival and completion observed and has no protocol violations. Every step's sandbox_check pid is its own actor's pid and its order is 'query_first'. Every extension event has result_published True and belongs to its phase's actor. normalized_outcome is 'finished'. (2) Principal run, through chain(). by_id requires exactly one event or step for a_issue, b_issue, b_consume_first, c_consume_second, c_release and b_release, and for each read step. Token refs ta and tb, delivery refs db and dc, and handle refs hb and hc must exist, or a KeyError follows. Every read must have result_source 'worker'. The associations are asserted: delivery dc carries token 'tb', c_consume uses delivery 'dc', and b_issue's actor_id is 'B'. A successful (rc 0) read whose name ends in 'after' must report the inode of the prepared target. The target bytes must be unchanged after the run. (3) Calibration: actor A unapplied, actor B applying C_POLICY, one hop. It asserts that a_issue native_nonnull is True, the transfer is delivered and equal, b_consume is 'returned' with native_result != -1, B's read before consuming fails (rc != 0), and B's read after consuming succeeds (rc 0) with matching bytes. (4) Contrasts. Each must pass apparatus_complete, which includes checking that the modified policy bytes were the ones applied. Each policy string edit must actually change the policy (asserts no_issue_allowance != B_POLICY and no_predicate != C_POLICY). Every step must have a worker result_source. For the two omit_* contrasts the script asserts 'not complete and not credited'.
tests.recorded_only: The script records but never asserts the following, and the run passes either way. The principal 'credited' flag and first_break: whether re-delegation actually worked is only written to report.json and printed. Every link's status, native_result, errno, custody and unavailable_reason. issued_by_pid, which is only looked up from the event's own actor_id, so it is not independent evidence of which process issued. The control reads (b_control_before, c_control_before), for which no expectation is set either way. The identity of any successful 'before' read. Release outcomes. Environment, policy hashes and pids. For the remove_b_issuance_allowance and omit_c_extension_predicate contrasts, credited, the events, reads and comparison text are only recorded. The comment that a usable chain 'would contradict' the removed dependency is never enforced. Note also that first_break does not cover equality, the baseline reads or the C-before read, so credited can be False while first_break is None, and the summary would print 'first break at None'. For the omit_* contrasts, 'not credited' follows automatically from 'not complete', because chain() is only evaluated when complete. So that assertion only checks that the product did not publish events for steps the spec removed.
fails_on: the envelope fails contract validation or the lifecycle-oracle record check
two actors share a pid (e.g. actors run in one process), an actor is not a child of the runner, exits non-zero or is not reaped
equipment is resolved differently from the request, is unsatisfied, unmatched or ineligible, runs under a different pid, or its binding is not packaged and inventory_verified
a policy is applied twice or not at all, its received or applied hash differs from the intended source, or the unapplied actor A reports an application
a phase's arrival or completion is not observed, or a protocol violation is recorded
a sandbox check runs against another actor's pid, or the order is not 'query_first'
any extension event is unpublished or attributed to the wrong actor
normalized_outcome is not 'finished' for any of the six runs

a principal event or step is missing or duplicated, or a token, delivery or handle record (ta/tb/db/dc/hb/hc) is absent, e.g. the product drops the 'tb' record when B's issue returns NULL; this crashes with a KeyError instead of recording a break
the second delivery is bound to A's token 'ta', C's consume names a delivery other than dc, or b_issue is attributed to an actor other than B
a read's result_source is not 'worker'
a successful after-read opens a file with a different inode than the prepared target
the target file is modified during the principal run

on this host: calibration issuance returns NULL, the transfer is not delivered or not equal, the consume returns -1, B's baseline read succeeds under C_POLICY, or the after-read fails or returns different bytes
the product fabricates an event for a step removed by omit_b_consume or omit_c_consume
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'this test shows that re-delegation works (B can re-issue an extension it consumed from A, and C can then read the target)', or 'the contrasts show the issuance allowance and the extension predicate are necessary'. Not supported: principal crediting, and crediting in the two policy-weakened contrasts, are only recorded and printed, never asserted. The omit_* assertions are satisfied structurally once the omitted events are absent. Also not supported: that issued_by_pid independently proves B's process issued, because it is derived from actor_id. That A is 'unentitled', because the code checks only that A's equipment matches the spec. That the control reads show the grant is limited to the target, because they carry no assertion. And the calibration exercises only one hop, with C_POLICY on B, not re-delegation.

tests.asserted: Five assertion groups run inside check(), which catches only AssertionError, KeyError, TypeError and ValueError, records pass or fail in assertions.json and prints PASS or FAIL. The final line, assert all(passed), makes the script fail if any group failed; there is no xfail mode. The groups for the pre_apply run (SeamCapture scenario pre_apply.pre_ready_timeout, overrides worker_pre_ready_hang_ms=10000 and worker_timeout_ms=200) are as follows. (1) file_effects: both seeded files are unchanged. (2) evidence: consumer.validate returns no errors. Every row is observation 'unavailable' with basis no_completed_worker_result, order 'unestablished', 'attempt:not_reached' among its limitations, a synthetic sandbox_check with missing_reason validator_not_invoked, attempt missing_reason slot_incomplete, and null errno and native_rc. CLI rc is 1, kind is 'run', result.ok is False, and the controller and runner outcomes agree. runner.rc is the int 1. specimen_id and test_overrides are echoed. runner.pid equals the worker pid. The ordering flags (collection_closed_before_proceed, proceed_set, proceed_observed, worker_lifetime_established) are all False, protocol_violations is empty, validator_disposition is 'not_invoked'. sandboxed_after_apply is not True. There is no validator subprocess. partial_steps is True. The worker died with term_signal 9 and exit_code None. The error mentions pw-probe-runner. Every prediction outcome is a non-empty string that is neither 'allow' nor 'deny'. Every attempt has outcome no_completed_result, errno None and the requested path. (3) lifecycle: no ready byte, done not observed, poll_stop_reason sentinel_deadline, exit_requested, reaped, no wait_errors, and a termination_request with signal 9, rc 0 and no errno. (4) no_policy_cause: the outcome is not runner_sandbox_denied; any diagnostics have cause and termination_cause in {None, unknown, undetermined, CAUSE_LABELS}; sandbox_caused_termination and policy_caused_termination are not True; none of the four 'sandbox killed'-type phrases appears. (5) outcome_attribution: the runner and controller outcomes are not in {finished, sandbox_apply_failed, bad_policy, runner_sandbox_denied}. (6) library_result_attribution: library_claims() finds no apply or compile rc/errno fields and no matching prose. The positive_control run uses the same files, plan and policy with no overrides. It asserts: allowed write changed file 0 to non-empty different bytes, and file 1 is unchanged. consumer.select returns step 0 as succeeded and step 1 as permission_failure with permission_errno. rc is 0, ok is True, outcome 'finished', sandboxed_after_apply True. The worker exited 0 with no signal and partial_steps False. A separate validator subprocess exists with a different pid and exit 0. validate_step reports no failures. Each prediction has the worker's pid, file-write-data, the target as filter_value and rc == step index. Step 0 is ok on the target with no errno. Step 1 is open_failed with rc 1, errno EPERM or EACCES, and 'open(' in the error. The lifecycle group asserts done, no termination_request, and the no-cause checks. The no_worker block uses hard asserts outside check(): files unchanged, rc 1, outcome worker_spawn_failed, 'posix_spawn' in the error, overrides echoed, no runner_subprocess or validator, no top-level 'ordering' key, every order unestablished, and the envelope is valid. The argv-refusal block, also hard asserts, runs for four out-of-range overrides. Running the bundled worker directly must exit 2 with the flag name and 'out of range' on stderr. The CLI run must leave the request file and seeded files unchanged, return rc 1 with runner_failed at both levels, echo the override, carry no request_failure, show a child that was reaped with exit 2 and no signal, no ready byte and no done, never sandboxed, no validator, every step no_completed_result and unestablished, no library claims, and a valid envelope.
tests.recorded_only: Several outputs are only written to files. prediction_observations.json holds producer, validator_subprocess and predictions per run; producer is never asserted anywhere. There are file .before and .after copies, effects.json, native.stdout, native.stderr and native-command.json, and assertions.json with its PASS/FAIL lines. Neither the specific pre_apply outcome value nor the specific non-allow/deny prediction outcome string is pinned: any value outside the forbidden set, or any non-empty string, passes. The comment 'the seam is after compilation, before readiness/application' is not checked; nothing asserts that compilation happened. Not every assertion is collected. An exception type other than the four caught ones (e.g. IndexError from runner['phases'][0], AttributeError) aborts the script immediately. Setup failures and the no_worker and argv-refusal asserts are also immediate hard failures, so the 'every group runs' promise covers only the check() groups.
fails_on: the pre-apply run reports 'finished', 'bad_policy', 'sandbox_apply_failed' or 'runner_sandbox_denied', or returns CLI rc 0 or result.ok true

the reply contains non-null apply_rc, apply_errno, compile_rc or compile_errno, an operation-tagged record (sandbox_apply/compile/5/8...) with an rc or errno, or prose like 'sandbox_apply returned -1'
diagnostics name a sandbox or policy cause outside the allowed labels, set sandbox_caused_termination or policy_caused_termination true, or say 'killed by sandbox'
pre-apply steps get an allow/deny prediction, a populated errno or native_rc, an established order, or lack 'attempt:not_reached'
the reply claims proceed or collection-closed, a validator was invoked, sandboxed_after_apply is True, or a ready byte was received
the pre-apply worker is not killed by SIGKILL (has an exit code), the termination request is missing or its kill rc is non-zero, poll_stop_reason is not sentinel_deadline, or the worker is not reaped
the pre-apply run changes either seeded file

positive control: the allowed write leaves bytes unchanged or empty, the denied write changes bytes, the denial errno is not EPERM or EACCES, prediction rc is not 0 for allow and 1 for deny, the validator shares the worker's pid or exits non-zero, or test_overrides are echoed when none were sent
a missing worker executable is reported as something other than worker_spawn_failed, the error lacks 'posix_spawn', a runner_subprocess is fabricated, or a top-level ordering object appears
the native worker accepts an out-of-range override (exit not 2, or no 'out of range' message)
the CLI refuses an out-of-range override at request decoding (request_failure present) instead of launching the worker, or the launched child exits other than 2, or the request file is mutated
the envelope fails consumer.validate in any run
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'the pre-apply run proves the worker compiled the policy and never applied it'. Not supported: no compilation evidence is asserted. Non-application is inferred only from the reply not claiming it (sandboxed_after_apply may be None or missing), from the missing ready byte, and from the unchanged files. Other claims it does not support: (1) that library_claims catches every library-result claim; it matches fixed field names and a regex, and its own docstring says it must be extended for other names. (2) That the no_worker run has 'no ordering object at all'; only a top-level 'ordering' key is checked, while ordering elsewhere lives at phases[0].ordering. (3) That the CLI-launched worker refused for the same argv reason; only its exit code 2 is compared, and its stderr is not checked. (4) That every assertion group always runs; this holds only for the four caught exception types inside check().

tests.asserted: For every row in the fixture tests/fixtures/contract/compiled_profile.json, the test builds a synthetic worker reply with outcome 'finished' and sets compiled_profile to the row's receipt. It decodes that reply with serde as PWRunnerRunResult ('retained'), then passes it through observe_reply, the production orchestration with a supplied client result. Per row it asserts: (1) exactly one client call; (2) the outgoing request does not contain the substring 'capture'; (3) the policy-check helper received no input; (4) the exit code is 0 if the row is valid and 1 otherwise, and wire result.exit_code matches; (5) result.ok equals valid; (6) normalized_outcome is 'finished' if valid and 'malformed_runner_response' otherwise; (7) data.runner_result decodes to exactly the test's retained value, Some or None; (8) data.policy_check is present and null; (9) the runner_sandbox_diagnostics key is present. Then by branch. Valid rows: diagnostics is an object and result.error is null. Invalid rows that the test's typed decode accepted: diagnostics null, runner_reply_error null, and result.error exactly 'unsupported or malformed compiled_profile' for the row named status_future, otherwise exactly 'compiled_profile context is inconsistent'. Invalid rows the decode rejected: diagnostics null, runner_result null, runner_reply_error a string, and result.error equal to it. Finally the admitted labels are exactly ['captured','unavailable'] in fixture order, and the counts (by_admission, by_reader) are exactly (9, 8). The scratch directory must be removable.
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is only recorded; every check is an assertion. But much of what the comments say rests on fixture content this test never inspects: that admission 'reads a receipt's status and its two labels and nothing else'; which fields are the 'two labels'; that the 8 reader-refused rows carry a non-string or absent status or label; and that the admitted 'captured' row's nonce, source and parameter fields disagree with the request. Whether each row goes to the by_admission or by_reader branch is decided by the test's own serde decode, not by observing where the product refused it. Nothing asserts that a row named status_future exists or that it falls in the admission branch. The contents of the valid rows' diagnostics object are not checked.
fails_on: an invalid receipt is admitted (exit 0, ok true, finished), or a valid one ('captured' or 'unavailable') is refused, e.g. by refusing 'captured' because its nonce, source or parameters do not match the request
refusals report an outcome other than malformed_runner_response, or an exit code or result.exit_code other than 1
on refusal the envelope drops a structurally decodable runner_result, or returns one that differs from the typed decode, or invents one when decoding failed
the fallback policy-check helper is invoked, or data.policy_check is missing or non-null
the client is called more than once (e.g. a retry), or the request contains 'capture'
the runner_sandbox_diagnostics key is omitted, is non-null on a refused row, or is not an object on an admitted row
an admission refusal fills runner_reply_error, or a reader refusal lacks a string runner_reply_error or reports a different result.error
the refusal message text differs from the two exact strings, or status_future gets the 'inconsistent' message
the fixture or the decode type changes so that the admitted list, its order, or the 9/8 split differs
a fixture row lacks name, valid or receipt (unwrap panic)
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'admission depends on the status and two labels and nothing else'. Not supported: the test only checks the outcome for each of the 19 fixture rows. It does not vary other receipt fields while holding status and labels fixed, and it cannot show the fixture's 'captured' row actually disagrees with the request, because it never inspects that content. Also not supported: 'the product's admission check rejects all 17 bad receipts'. The 8 by_reader rows fail typed decoding before admission, so admission is never exercised on them. And the receipts come from a synthetic worker("finished") reply, not from a real worker.

tests.asserted: Setup: the synthetic app has an augment read_control.sb containing '(deny file-read-data)'. The request file contains runner.mode 'standard', policy source '(version 1) (allow default)' and augments ['read_control']. run_held runs production run() with Form::Run, using an injected client callback and policy-check helper. The client callback overwrites the request file with REPLACEMENT and returns its preset result exactly once; a second client call panics on expect. After run(), the file must equal REPLACEMENT. First run, where the client returns client_run(None) and no typed reply: exactly one client input, which parses to JSON equal to the hand-written expected object (contract, specimen_id, policy {format sbpl, sbpl_source '(version 1) (allow default)\n(deny file-read-data)'}, probe_plan []), so the runner selector and the augments key are gone and the augment is spliced in with a newline. The helper was called at least once, and every helper input is byte-identical to the client input. data.policy_check equals the serialized capture the stub returns for that input, including the input's sha256. actor_policy_checks is absent. Exit code is 1, normalized_outcome is 'xpc_error', and runner_result and runner_sandbox_diagnostics are present and null. Second run, with the same request rewritten, client_run(Some(reply)) and a fixture_reply: the client input equals the first run's input exactly, the helper input list is empty, policy_check is present and null, outcome is 'finished', and exit is 0.
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is only recorded. Some things are outside the assertions. The helper is a stub that returns status 'ok' for any input, so the fallback compilation itself is never exercised; the test's own comment says it does not show that the shipped client or helper behaves this way. The number of helper calls is not pinned, only that there is at least one. The order of the helper call relative to the client call is not recorded. Whether the product checks the capture's controlled_input_sha256 against the input is not exercised; only a matching digest is supplied. REPLACEMENT's contents are not visible here, so the code does not show they differ from the original request in a way that would expose a re-read.
fails_on: the client receives the raw request: the runner selector is kept, the augments key is kept, the augment is not spliced, or it is spliced with a different separator (sbpl_source is compared exactly)
the client is invoked more than once (expect panic or inputs.len() != 1)
on xpc failure no fallback helper call happens

the helper receives bytes that differ from the client's input, e.g. the controller re-reads the replaced request file after the client call, or re-serializes the held request (different key order or whitespace), since the comparison is byte-for-byte
the envelope's policy_check is missing, rewritten, truncated or taken from a different input
actor_policy_checks appears for an ordinary run
the no-reply run does not report exit 1 and 'xpc_error', or omits the runner_result or runner_sandbox_diagnostics keys or makes them non-null
the helper is called even though the client delivered a reply, or policy_check is non-null or missing in that run
the delivered-reply run is not 'finished' with exit 0, or its client input differs from the first run's
run() returns Err, or the request file is not REPLACEMENT afterwards (e.g. the client was never invoked)
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'the fallback compiles the correct, held policy' or 'the shipped helper compiles this input'. Not supported: the helper is a stub that always answers 'ok', and the comment itself disclaims the shipped client and helper. Also not supported: that the helper is called after the file replacement (call order is not asserted; byte equality would hold even if the helper ran first), that it is called exactly once, or that the controller never reads the request file again. The test only shows that the helper's input equals the client's input, and its power to catch a re-read depends on REPLACEMENT differing from the request, which this file does not show.

tests.asserted: Hard assertions, any of which fails the script. (1) classifier_controls: all 16 constructed samples classify as expected: ALIVE, EXITED or RELEASED, or refuse with Unresolved or InvalidObservation. This tests the checker's own classifier, not the product. (2) Live setup: P and C are both in the process group whose id is P's pid; control.assert_running() passes; both helper paths resolve to the helper; C's ppid is P; P's parent process is named pw-probe-runner and its identity is unchanged on re-snapshot. (3) After both streams are closed and P is told to exit, P's kqueue exit event arrives within 2 s. (4) classify_lifetime on the post-CLI sample must settle: Unresolved or InvalidObservation propagates and fails the run. So the CLI's exit event must arrive within 25 s of the leader's exit. The exit watch must have been registered before completion was triggered. C must either have an exit event, or acknowledge a ping with a readable snapshot that has the same pid, start time, path and process group. (5) run.load_json() must succeed. (6) After release, control.assert_stopped(timeout=3) must pass. If the history was ALIVE, a second sample must classify as RELEASED, meaning an exit event is observed after the release. (7) cleanup must record no errors when there is no primary error: helper exits known for exactly P and C, the worker (pw-probe-runner) observed to exit within 5 s, the CLI closed, cleanup.json written and staging removed. Otherwise it raises AssertionError.
tests.recorded_only: The checker deliberately gives no verdict on the descendant's lifetime. ALIVE (alive_acknowledged) and EXITED (exited_before_cleanup) both pass; account.json stores verdict None, and termination_cause is fixed as 'not identified'. reply_account compares 26 product claims, but a mismatch only becomes a disagreement and a favorable or unfavorable judgment in account.json. Those claims include CLI rc 0, consumer.validate errors (so contract-validation failures are not fatal here), outcome 'finished', the runner_subprocess fields, the exec attempt fields, the assert_observation result (caught and turned into a string), stdout and the later step's fields. The later file effect (target == b'x') is also judged only. Also recorded: rc, elapsed time, exit stamps, ping timings, exit_minus_cli_completion_ns, before_cli_completion vs at_or_after, exit_events_after_release, and interventions_before_sampling, which is never filled so it is always []. Whether the enclosing case fails on an unfavorable judgment is not settled by this file. The exit stamps are the times the checker observed the events, and events returned in one wake share a stamp, so 'before_cli_completion' can be misclassified as at or after.
fails_on: the CLI does not exit within 25 s after the leader exits, e.g. the product waits for the whole process group or the surviving descendant after leader exit and EOF (Unresolved)
the leader P does not produce an exit event within 2 s of the trigger
P is not a process-group leader containing C, or P's parent is not pw-probe-runner (e.g. spawned through an intermediate process)
C's identity or process group changes between registration and sampling (InvalidObservation)
C neither exits (event) nor acknowledges a ping, e.g. the product stops or suspends the group, or the ping succeeds but the snapshot is unreadable (Unresolved)
after release, the helpers do not stop within 3 s, or a descendant that was ALIVE gives no exit event (RELEASED not reached)
the pw-probe-runner worker does not exit within 5 s during cleanup, or the CLI cannot be closed, so staging is retained and cleanup raises
the CLI produces no parseable JSON (load_json raises)
the checker's own classifier gives a wrong result on a constructed control
tests.unsupported_claim: Claim: 'the product reports the exec truthfully (leader_exit_and_eof, rc 0, finished)' or 'the later step wrote its byte'. Not supported: reply disagreements and the file effect are only judged and written to account.json, and the run passes with an 'unfavorable' judgment. Also not supported: any claim that the product kills, or leaves alive, same-group descendants. Both histories pass, no verdict is given, and the cause of an exit is explicitly not identified, because the kqueue event carries no status for a non-child. The 'before/after CLI completion' detail is not reliable ordering either, because stamps are observation times and events in one wake share a stamp. And a CLI that exits on its own 30 s timeout could still fall inside the 25 s window if setup took more than about 5 s.

tests.asserted: Scheduler run for a two-actor token scenario (A issues, self-transfers, transfers to B; A consumes later; B consumes twice then releases twice). Fails unless: no cancellation; all three visits end 'completed'; both transfers acknowledged delivered with recipients [0,1]; B's inbound slot acknowledgement read at phase 1 equals PWAuthorityAck.accepted (delivery accepted while B was parked); B's completedSlotCount was 0 at that moment (the code comments it as phase 0 end, but the callback reads it when phase==1 begins); b_first, b_again and a_consume completed with callBoundary and unavailableCode 0; each release is completed and its unavailableCode is 2 if the matching consume's nativeResult was -1, else 0; and custody's erased flags equal exactly [true] (one custody record, erased).
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is merely recorded in the test body: the phase callback captures values, but they are then asserted. The raw native consume results are read only to derive the expected release unavailableCode and are not themselves asserted (consume may return -1 or not, and the test accepts either as long as the release code matches). The 'distinct lifecycle references even when raw handles agree' comment is explanatory only; handle values are never compared.
fails_on: Worker binary missing (throws TestFailure)
Any visit ending in a reason other than completed, or cancellation
B's delivery not accepted by phase 1 (e.g. acknowledged only after B runs, or still pending)
B consuming anything before its phase arrives (completedSlotCount != 0)
Self-transfer to A's own inbound slot not delivered, or recipient indices differing from [0,1]
A consume or B consume marked unavailable (unavailableCode != 0) or not completed / no call boundary
Second B release reporting the wrong unavailable code relative to its consume result (e.g. releasing the first handle's reference twice, or a release that should report 2 reporting 0)
Custody not erased, erased too many/few records, or erased flag false after the last declared transfer
tests.unsupported_claim: That custody is erased AT the token's last declared transfer (as the comment says), or that erasure is timely. The test only checks the final erased flag in the outcome after the whole run, so it cannot distinguish erasure at the transfer from erasure at the end of the run. It also does not prove the kernel/native consume succeeded (-1 is tolerated), nor that handles are distinct (raw handle values are never compared), nor that a parked recipient could not consume (it only shows B had consumed nothing by phase 1 under this schedule).

tests.asserted: Apparatus assertions on every run (principal, calibration, four contrasts): envelope validates and passes lifecycle oracle; execution_form actors; worker exit witnessed; actor set matches spec; distinct pids; per-actor equipment requested==resolved, satisfied, matched/eligible, packaged binding with inventory_verified identity; subprocess reaped with exit 0 and parent pid equals runner pid; applied actors applied exactly once with policy hash equal to the spec and received hash, unapplied actors declared unapplied with count 0; phases arrival/completion observed and no protocol violations; every step's sandbox_check pid matches its actor and comparison order is query_first; every extension event published and attributed to the phase's actor; normalized_outcome finished. In the principal: second delivery is bound to token 'tb' and delivery 'dc', the second issue was by actor B, successful reads' fresh-descriptor inode equals the prepared target inode, target file unchanged. Calibration asserts hard: A's issue native_nonnull True, transfer delivered and equal, B consume returned and not -1, B's read before fails (rc != 0) and after succeeds with matching bytes. Contrasts assert hard only for omit_b_consume and omit_c_consume: the chain is incomplete and not credited.
tests.recorded_only: The principal's 'credited' flag, first_break, every link status, and read outcomes are computed and written to report.json and printed, not asserted; a principal run with the chain broken (NULL issue, failed consume, denied read) still passes as long as the apparatus assertions hold, and the printed summary just says 'not credited, first break at X'. For remove_b_issuance_allowance and omit_c_extension_predicate the code only records a 'comparison' label string and the observed events/reads; nothing is asserted about whether the chain is credited or whether issue/read succeeded. Control reads (b/c_control_before) are recorded with no expectation. The print line claims calibration 'exercised' issue, transfer, consume and access, which is true only because the calibration asserts passed beforehand.
fails_on: Any apparatus fault: envelope or lifecycle invalid, fewer or duplicate pids, wrong equipment resolution or binding, an actor not reaped or exiting nonzero, policy applied zero or two times, hash mismatch, unapplied actor reporting applied, phase protocol violation, step order not query_first, unpublished extension event, outcome not finished
Principal chain wiring wrong: second delivery bound to A's token instead of tb, or second issue not run by B
A successful after-read whose fresh descriptor inode is not the prepared target, or the target file modified
Calibration: issuance refused (NULL), transfer not delivered/equal, B consume failing or -1, B's pre-read succeeding, or post-read failing or returning wrong bytes (positive coverage missing)
omit_b_consume or omit_c_consume contrast where all six link events are still present or the chain gets credited
tests.unsupported_claim: That the test proves re-delegation works (or that the kernel permits it, or that policy changes caused C's read). The principal chain outcome is not asserted at all, so a green run is consistent with re-delegation failing; credit is only reported. Likewise the two policy-weakening contrasts assert nothing about their outcome, so they do not show that the issuance allowance or extension predicate is necessary. Calibration shows only that a single A-to-B issue/transfer/consume/read works on the host, not three-actor re-delegation.

tests.asserted: Several independent assertion groups run through check() which catches AssertionError/KeyError/TypeError/ValueError, records pass/fail to assertions.json, and a final assert fails if any group failed (no xfail). Pre-apply failure run (worker hangs before ready, 200ms sentinel, SIGKILL): files unchanged; envelope valid; CLI rc 1, result.ok False; every step has synthetic unavailable observation, order unestablished, 'attempt:not_reached', missing_reason validator_not_invoked / slot_incomplete, null errno; runner rc 1; test_overrides equal controls; worker pid positive and equals runner pid; ordering flags (collection closed, proceed, lifetime established all False; validator not_invoked; no protocol violations); worker partial_steps True, term_signal 9, exit_code None; error mentions pw-probe-runner; attempt outcome 'no_completed_result', requested_path matches; prediction outcome a non-empty string not allow/deny; no sandboxed_after_apply; no validator subprocess; lifecycle: no ready byte, done not observed, poll_stop_reason sentinel_deadline, exit requested, reaped, no wait errors, termination_request signal 9 rc 0; no sandbox/policy cause claim; normalized_outcome (runner and controller) not in {finished, sandbox_apply_failed, bad_policy, runner_sandbox_denied}; no library compile/apply result claims anywhere in runner or controller summary. Positive control (same files, seeds, policy and plan, real worker): rc 0, ok, outcome finished, sandboxed_after_apply, worker exit 0, validator separate pid exit 0, step 0 allowed and succeeded (sandbox rc 0, file changed to nonempty different bytes), step 1 denied (sandbox rc 1, open_failed, errno EPERM/EACCES, file bytes unchanged), validate_step passes, query_first order. Also a no_worker run (bad executable path: rc 1, worker_spawn_failed, posix_spawn in error, no subprocess, no ordering, files unchanged) and four argv-refusal cases (native worker exits 2 with 'out of range' naming the flag; CLI path yields runner_failed, child exit 2, no ready byte, files unchanged, request file unchanged).
tests.recorded_only: prediction_observations.json records producer, validator_subprocess and per-step sandbox_check predictions for both runs without asserting them beyond the specific checks above; the stdout/stderr of the native argv runs and before/after file bytes are saved as artifacts; assertions.json records pass/fail per group (the recording itself is not a verdict, but the final assert converts any failure into a test failure). In the pre-apply run the prediction outcome is only required to be a non-empty string that is not allow/deny; its actual value is not pinned.
fails_on: Pre-apply run modifying either target file
Pre-apply outcome reported as finished, bad_policy, sandbox_apply_failed or runner_sandbox_denied, or any reported apply/compile rc/errno/'compile returned' claim
Diagnostics attributing the kill to the sandbox or policy, or cause labels outside the allowed set
Pre-apply run claiming the worker became ready, sent done, or reporting a validator, or a different signal than 9 / exit_code not None
Predictions reported as allow/deny when no query ran, or attempt outcome other than no_completed_result
Positive control not allowing step 0 / denying step 1 with EPERM or EACCES, or writing to the denied file
Failed spawn run having an ordering object or changing files
Native worker accepting out-of-range arguments, or CLI path not mapping them to runner_failed
tests.unsupported_claim: That the sandbox or policy policy application failed, hung or caused the worker's death (or that compilation succeeded/failed). The test asserts the opposite: no library or cause claim may be reported, and the fault is injected by a test seam (hang before readiness) so the failure is synthetic. It also does not show where the worker was when killed beyond the report fields, nor does it show real-world pre-apply failures occur; the code even says the outcome names only the missing completed result and not whether the operation started.

tests.asserted: Through production orchestration with a supplied client result, for each receipt in a fixture corpus (include_str corpus; the test comment says two admitted, seventeen refused): exactly one client call whose request lacks 'capture'; no helper inputs; exit code 0 and ok true iff the case's valid flag, else 1/false; wire exit_code equals process exit; normalized_outcome finished if valid else malformed_runner_response; the wire runner_result equals the structurally decoded reply if it decodes (else retained None via Option equality); policy_check null; diagnostics key present. Valid rows: diagnostics an object, no result error; admitted list must be exactly ['captured','unavailable']. Invalid rows that decode: diagnostics null, runner_reply_error null, result error string equals 'unsupported or malformed compiled_profile' for status_future, otherwise 'compiled_profile context is inconsistent'. Invalid rows that do not decode: diagnostics null, runner_result null, reply error is a string and equals result error. Final counts must be (9 refused by admission, 8 refused by the typed reader). Scratch root removed.
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is merely printed. But the corpus contents are not visible: which receipt fields make rows valid or invalid is hidden in the fixture JSON. The split into by_admission/by_reader is derived by whether the test's own typed deserialization succeeds, then counted and asserted against fixed numbers, so it records how the typed reader behaves as much as the admission rule. The 'captured' row deliberately mismatches the request's no-capture and is admitted; that is asserted only through the admitted list and exit code, not by any direct comparison of nonce/source/params.
fails_on: Admitting any corpus row the fixture marks invalid, or refusing captured/unavailable
Wrong error text for a decoded-but-refused row (status_future vs the other label cases)
Admission looking at fields other than status and the two labels in a way that changes a verdict (would change which rows are valid, though that is judged only via fixture flags)
Runner result dropped or altered for a decoded refused reply (structurally decoded reports must remain available)
Refused row leaving non-null diagnostics, or a policy_check being non-null, or a helper being invoked, or a second client call, or the request gaining a capture
Malformed-type rows (non-string status/label) not surfacing a string reply error that equals the result error
Any change in the 9/8 split or the admitted set
tests.unsupported_claim: That reply admission reads ONLY status and the two labels and ignores nonce/source/parameter fields (the test name and comments say this). The test cannot show that: it only has one admitted row that mismatches the request, and refusal reasons are not shown to depend on exactly those fields since the fixture is invisible. Nor does it show that the production reader (as opposed to this test's typed reader) refuses the eight non-string rows, or that all 17 refusals are for the stated reasons; the 'nine/eight' split relies on the test's own serde decoding.

tests.asserted: Using run_held with injected client and helper callbacks (the request file is overwritten inside the client callback): in the first scenario (client reports no result), exactly one client invocation; the client's input parsed as JSON equals an independently authored expected request (selector 'runner' removed, augment read_control spliced into sbpl_source with a newline); at least one helper call, and every helper input is byte-identical to the client input; the envelope's policy_check equals the capture the helper stub returns for that input; no actor_policy_checks key; exit code 1; normalized_outcome xpc_error; runner_result and runner_sandbox_diagnostics null; the file on disk equals REPLACEMENT after the run (asserted in run_held). Second scenario with a delivered host reply: client input identical to the first, no helper calls, policy_check null, outcome finished, exit 0.
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is printed. Beyond that, helper behaviour is a stub returning a canned 'ok' capture that embeds the input hash; the capture is compared as an echo of the stub, so the comparison of policy_check merely shows the controller embeds the helper's answer. The test comment states that it does not show the shipped client reaches this capture nor that the shipped helper compiles the input.
fails_on: Controller giving the helper a re-read of the replaced file (REPLACEMENT bytes) or a differently serialized/resolved request than the client got
Held input not matching the authored expected (augment not spliced, selector left in, extra fields)
No helper call in the failure path, or helper input differing in even one byte
policy_check missing, altered, or built from something other than the helper's return
Helper being called when the client delivered a host reply
Wrong exit code or outcome in either path, or non-null runner_result/diagnostics in the no-reply path, or actor_policy_checks present
Controller overwriting or not leaving the replacement file intact
tests.unsupported_claim: That the real fallback policy compilation compiles or checks the policy actually run, or that the real client and helper behave this way. All collaborators are fakes, and the test's own comment disclaims this. It also does not show the fallback compiles the right input in the sense of semantic correctness of augment splicing in general, only equality for one augment, and the 'expected' is authored for this one request; and it does not show the helper input is immune to the file replacement beyond this single replace-in-callback ordering.

tests.asserted: main() unconditionally runs classifier_controls first, which asserts 16 constructed samples classify as expected (alive with ack ping; exit before/after CLI completion; ack ping then exit; unack ping then exit; exit after release; Unresolved cases for missing evidence, missing CLI exit, no exit after release; InvalidObservation for changed identity/group, watch registered after trigger, never registered, exit before registration). In the live run it asserts: process group of P and C are equal and equal P's pid; control stays running; helper paths match; C's parent is P; worker named pw-probe-runner and identity stable; leader exit event observed within 2s; classify_lifetime must return (not raise Unresolved/InvalidObservation), so the lifetime must be settled by registered exit events or ack ping plus matching identity and group, CLI exit event must exist, and the exit watch must precede the trigger; if ALIVE, a post-release resample must classify as exited_after_fixture_release; release leaves both helpers stopped; cleanup must confirm all exits or the case raises AssertionError ('cleanup observations') when no primary error.
tests.recorded_only: The descendant's history (alive vs exited), the exit timing relative to CLI completion, and the reply account are recorded and not judged: lifetime verdict is explicitly None and either ALIVE or EXITED passes. reply_account compares ~26 reported claims (cli rc, validation errors, outcome finished, exec fields, stdout text, leader pid, later step) to expectations and produces 'disagreements' and a favorable/unfavorable judgment, but these are written to account.json and printed as counts only; a disagreement does not raise. Likewise the later file effect (file equals b'x') is a judgment written to account.json, not asserted. Termination cause is recorded as not identified. observation_disagreement catches assert_observation failures into a string rather than failing.
fails_on: Classifier logic wrong on any of the 16 constructed controls
Helper fixture setup wrong (P and C not in same process group, C not child of P, helper path or worker name mismatch)
Leader exit not observed within 2s of the trigger, or CLI exit not observed within 25s (leaves Unresolved)
Descendant neither exit-observed nor ping-acknowledged with readable matching snapshot, or snapshot showing a different identity or group (Unresolved/InvalidObservation)
Post-release resample of a live descendant not yielding exited_after_fixture_release
Cleanup unable to confirm helper/worker/CLI exits (staging retained and AssertionError raised)
Any exception in the CLI launch/run or envelope loading (run.load_json); note envelope parsing happens after the lifetime classification
tests.unsupported_claim: That the product kills, leaves alone, or reaps the same-group descendant (or that the descendant survives/does not survive), or that the product's exec reply is truthful. The checker explicitly assigns no verdict to the lifetime (verdict=None), accepts either history, and the reply-versus-reality comparison only produces a recorded judgment, not a failure. The exit event also does not identify who/what terminated the descendant.

tests.asserted: Scheduler run with two actors (A issues a token, transfers it to itself and to B, later consumes the self-delivery; B consumes twice on one delivery then releases twice). Asserts: no cancellation; three visits all end 'completed'; both transfers acknowledged delivered with recipients [0,1]; at B's phase start (phase 1) B's inbound slot acknowledgement == accepted (so accepted while parked) and B's completedSlotCount == 0 (nothing consumed before its phase); b_first and b_again completed with callBoundary true and unavailableCode 0; each release completed with unavailableCode == (2 if its paired consume native result was -1 else 0); a_consume completed, callBoundary, unavailableCode 0; custody list maps to erased flags exactly [true] (one token, erased).
tests.recorded_only: The raw native results of the consumes are not asserted to any value (only used to derive the expected release unavailable code, so a result of -1 or not both pass). Raw handle values (handles 1 and 2 are distinct indices, but the comment says raw handles may agree) are not compared. The final erased flag is checked only as a boolean; the test does not show when or why erasure happened beyond the comment.
fails_on: B consumes before its release/phase (completedSlotCount != 0 at phase 1)
B's delivery not accepted while parked (ack != accepted at phase 1)
either transfer not acknowledged delivered, or wrong recipient order
a consume or release not completed / no call boundary / nonzero unavailable code on consume
a release whose unavailable code does not match its consume's result (e.g. 2 expected after a -1 consume, or nonzero after a success), i.e. repeated consume/release sharing a reference incorrectly
self-transfer delivery not consumable by A in a later visit
any visit ending other than completed, or a cancellation
custody erased flag false, or more/fewer than one custody record
tests.unsupported_claim: That the kernel/real extension consume succeeds, or that repeated consume returns the same result: native results are unconstrained. Also that erasure happened exactly at the last transfer (the assertion only shows erased==true at the end of the run, with one record); also that references are distinct at the kernel level, only the release unavailability pattern is checked.

tests.asserted: Apparatus assertions via apparatus_complete for principal, calibration and every contrast: envelope/lifecycle validation clean, execution_form actors, worker exit witnessed, distinct actor pids, equipment requested==resolved, satisfied and matched, policy applied exactly once with matching sha256 for B and C and A unapplied, phases arrival/completion observed with no protocol violations, step sandbox_check pid matches actor and query_first order, events result_published, normalized_outcome finished. Principal: B_to_C delivery bound to token tb, C consume delivery dc, b_issue actor B; fresh-read identity inode equals prepared target for successful 'after' reads; target bytes unchanged. Calibration (hard asserts): A issue native_nonnull True, transfer delivered and equal, B consume returned and result != -1, before read rc != 0, after read rc == 0 with matching bytes. Contrasts: omit_b_consume and omit_c_consume must have an incomplete link set and not be credited.
tests.recorded_only: Principal chain outcome: whether A/B issue are non-null, consume results, errno, read rc values for before/after, and the 'credited' re-delegation verdict and first_break are written to report.json and printed, not asserted; the principal can be not credited and the script still passes. Contrasts remove_b_issuance_allowance and omit_c_extension_predicate record observed events/reads/credited with only a free-text 'comparison' label and no assertion on the outcome. Control reads are recorded. Environment info is recorded.
fails_on: any apparatus defect: wrong pid count, policy not applied once or hash mismatch, unapplied A showing applied, protocol violations, unpublished events, non-'finished' outcome
calibration where issuance returns NULL, transfer not delivered/equal, consume fails (-1), before-read succeeds or after-read fails or bytes mismatch (host cannot do extensions, coverage missing)
principal b_to_c token not tb, c_consume delivery not dc, b_issue not by actor B
a successful principal after-read whose inode differs from the target
target file mutated
omit_b_consume or omit_c_consume contrasts that still report all six links or are credited
by_id lookups matching zero or multiple items
tests.unsupported_claim: That the test proves re-delegation works (or is blocked) in the kernel: the principal verdict is only recorded. Also that the two policy-weakening contrasts demonstrate their link is necessary: no assertion on their outcome, only recorded for comparison. Even the omit contrasts only show the checker's own credit logic refuses a chain with missing events, which is nearly tautological, not kernel behaviour.

tests.asserted: Assertion groups (each run, failures collected into assertions.json, final assert fails if any group failed) for a real run where the worker is hung before ready and killed by sentinel deadline (pre_apply) versus a positive control with the same files/policy/plan. Pre_apply asserts: file bytes unchanged; CLI rc 1, result.ok false, runner rc 1; every step comparison unavailable/no_completed_worker_result, order unestablished, synthetic sandbox_check with missing_reason validator_not_invoked, attempt slot_incomplete, null errno/rc; ordering flags (collection closed, proceed, worker lifetime all false, validator not_invoked, no protocol violations); no validator subprocess; worker partial_steps true, term_signal 9, exit_code None, error mentions pw-probe-runner; prediction outcome a non-empty string not allow/deny; attempt outcome no_completed_result, errno None, requested_path matches; lifecycle: ready byte not received, done not observed, poll_stop_reason sentinel_deadline, exit requested, reaped, no wait errors, termination_request signal 9 rc 0; no sandbox/policy cause claims in diagnostics (cause labels restricted, sandbox_caused flags not True, no prose like 'sandbox killed'); normalized_outcome (runner and controller) not in forbidden set {finished, sandbox_apply_failed, bad_policy, runner_sandbox_denied}; no library apply/compile result fields or prose claims. Positive control asserts: allowed write changes file and denied write leaves seed; step 0 allow/ok, step 1 deny/open_failed with EPERM/EACCES; validator pid distinct, exit 0; finished, sandboxed_after_apply true, worker exit 0. Also: no_worker case (nonexistent executable -> rc 1, worker_spawn_failed, no ordering, no runner_subprocess); four argv-refusal cases (native worker exit code 2 with 'out of range' on stderr, CLI runner_failed, exit_code 2, files unchanged, request file unchanged).
tests.recorded_only: observations (producer, validator_subprocess, predictions per step) written to prediction_observations.json; native stdout/stderr and command for argv refusal; file before/after copies; effects.json. The actual pre-apply normalized_outcome value is NOT pinned: only that it is not one of four forbidden spellings, so any other value (even e.g. runner_failed or an unknown string) passes. Prediction outcome for pre-apply is only required to be some non-empty string other than allow/deny.
fails_on: pre-apply run changing file bytes
a pre-apply report that claims allow/deny predictions, or claims the worker applied/compiled, or labels the outcome finished/bad_policy/sandbox_apply_failed/runner_sandbox_denied
attributing the termination to sandbox or policy
missing or wrong ordering flags, pid mismatch, missing term_signal 9
positive control not showing allow-then-deny with EPERM/EACCES or the allowed write not changing the file
spawn failure reporting an ordering object or a runner_subprocess
argv refusal not exiting 2 or CLI not reporting runner_failed, or files changed
consumer.validate returning errors
tests.unsupported_claim: That the test establishes what the correct normalized_outcome for a pre-apply failure is, or that the sandbox/policy was never applied: it only forbids four labels and absence of library-result claims, and the 'worker killed before apply' is inferred from ready byte not received plus no completed result, not directly observed. Also that the test shows the failure is robust to all pre-apply points: the hang is injected via one override seam after compilation.

tests.asserted: Over a fixture corpus of compiled_profile receipts (comment says 2 valid, 17 refused), through production orchestration with a supplied client reply, for every case: exactly one client call, request text contains no 'capture', no helper inputs, exit code 0 iff case valid else 1, wire exit_code/ok match, normalized_outcome 'finished' for valid and 'malformed_runner_response' otherwise, the wire runner_result equals the test's own typed decode of the reply, policy_check is null, diagnostics key present. Valid: diagnostics object and null error. Refused with decodable reply: diagnostics null, reply_error null, error text 'unsupported or malformed compiled_profile' only for label status_future, else 'compiled_profile context is inconsistent'. Refused where typed decode failed: runner_result null, reply_error string equal to result.error. Final: admitted names exactly ['captured','unavailable'] and split (9 by admission, 8 by reader).
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is merely printed; the counts are asserted. The fixture's content (which receipts are valid and why) is not visible here, only the 'valid' flag and names. The comment's claim that admission reads only status and the two labels is not itself asserted: the test shows these 19 corpus rows get the stated outcomes, not that other fields are ignored (beyond the 'captured' row, whose mismatching nonce/source/params is admitted).
fails_on: admitting any of the 17 refused receipts or refusing 'captured' or 'unavailable'
a different split than 9 admitted-by-reply-check refusals and 8 reader refusals (e.g. a refusal moving from reader to admission or reverse)
wrong error string for a refused-by-admission row (status_future vs others)
a refused row leaving non-null diagnostics, or an admitted row with null diagnostics or non-null error
helper being invoked or a second client call, or request containing capture
exit code or ok/normalized_outcome inconsistent with validity
runner_result not preserved for decodable refused replies
tests.unsupported_claim: That admission depends on status and labels 'alone' / ignores every other field: the test only shows one admitted row (captured) whose capture-related fields disagree with the request; it does not vary every other field independently. Also that the eight reader-refused rows are refused by the product's admission logic: the test says they are refused earlier by its own typed JSON reader, so they say nothing about admission, and the product's decoding of them is only seen as a reply_error string.

tests.asserted: Ordinary-form run via production orchestration with injected client and helper closures; request file is overwritten with REPLACEMENT inside the client callback. Asserts: the one client invocation's input parses to an independently authored expected JSON (augments selector removed, read_control augment text spliced after a newline); every helper input is byte-identical to the client input (so not the replaced file); the file ends as REPLACEMENT; envelope data.policy_check equals the wire form of capture_for(client input, 'ok'); no actor_policy_checks key; exit code 1 with normalized_outcome xpc_error; runner_result and runner_sandbox_diagnostics null. Second run with a delivered host reply: client input equals the first, no helper inputs, policy_check null, outcome finished, exit 0.
tests.recorded_only: The helper is a stub (answer returns a fabricated capture echoing the input's sha256), so its 'ok' status and digest are test-supplied and not evidence of compilation. The client is a stub as well. Nothing is printed. The test also does not assert how many times the helper was called (only non-empty).
fails_on: fallback input read from the file after replacement (re-reading the path) rather than the held request
client request not having selector removed or augment spliced as expected
helper input differing from the client input by even a byte
policy_check missing or different from the capture for that input, or present when a host reply was delivered
exit code or outcome different (xpc_error/1 on no reply, finished/0 with reply)
helper invoked when a reply is delivered, or actor_policy_checks present
request file not left as REPLACEMENT
tests.unsupported_claim: That the shipped client reaches this fallback or that the shipped helper compiles that input (the test's own comment disclaims it); also that the policy was really compiled or valid: helper and client are stubs and only input identity (held bytes, spliced augment) is checked. The sha256 in the capture is echoed from the helper input by the stub, so equality with it adds no independent evidence of compilation.

tests.asserted: Hard asserts: classifier_controls (16 constructed samples: alive with acknowledged ping, exit before/after CLI completion, acknowledged ping then exit, unacknowledged ping then exit, exit after fixture release; unresolved for missing evidence/ping/PID, missing CLI exit, no exit after release; invalid for changed identity/group, watch registered after trigger or never, exit before registration); live rendezvous: helpers P and C in same group led by P (pgid == P pid), C ppid == P, worker named pw-probe-runner, all exit watches registered before stream closure and leader exit; leader exit event observed within 2s; classify_lifetime must not raise (Unresolved or InvalidObservation propagate and fail the run), including requirement that the CLI exit event is seen; if the descendant is alive, after fixture release the same classifier must report exited_after_fixture_release; release leaves exit events; cleanup must confirm helper/worker exits and CLI close, otherwise AssertionError (unless a primary error exists).
tests.recorded_only: Descendant lifetime history (alive_acknowledged vs exited_before_cleanup) is recorded with verdict None, not asserted to either. The reply account (CLI rc, outcome finished, worker pid, exec rc, stdout text, exec_observation, later step) is compared to expectations, but disagreements are only turned into 'favorable'/'unfavorable' judgments in account.json and printed counts, not asserted; the later file effect (after bytes == b'x', != seed) likewise only a judgment. Observations, timing, process snapshots, cleanup records written to JSON.
fails_on: classifier mishandling any constructed sample (e.g. treating a missing ping as an exit, accepting a watch registered after trigger)
helper topology wrong (not same group, C not child of P, worker path not pw-probe-runner)
no leader exit event within 2s, or no CLI exit event within 25s (Unresolved)
descendant sample that cannot be classified (no exit event and no acknowledged ping, or identity/group changed)
alive descendant not later reported exited after release, or release not producing exit events
cleanup unable to confirm exits or close CLI, or cleanup write/remove errors
envelope validation or JSON loading errors (load_json/consumer.validate called in reply_account, errors would raise)
tests.unsupported_claim: That the product kills, leaves alone, or correctly reports the descendant, or that the reply is truthful: the lifetime verdict is deliberately None and reply disagreements do not fail the checker. Also that the product's exec account matches reality: only recorded as favorable/unfavorable. A pass establishes that the observation apparatus resolved the descendant's state, not that the product behaved correctly.

tests.asserted: Fails if: the worker binary is missing (TestFailure); the scheduler run is cancelled; any of three visits ends other than 'completed'; either transfer ack is not delivered, or recipients are not [0,1]; B's inbound delivery slot, sampled at the start of phase 1 while B is parked, is not PWAuthorityAck.accepted; B had completed any slot (count != 0) at that point; b_first, b_again or a_consume is not completed with callBoundary; their unavailableCode is not 0; each release is not completed, or its unavailableCode differs from (2 if the matching consume's nativeResult was -1, else 0); and custody erased flags are not exactly [true], i.e. one custody record, erased.
tests.recorded_only: The raw native results of the consumes are read but not compared to any fixed value (they only choose the expected release unavailableCode, so the release check is conditional, not a fixed outcome). The handle indices 1 and 2 are plan-side labels; the test never compares actual handle values or reference identity, so the comment 'distinct lifecycle references even when raw handles agree' is not directly asserted. The erased flag is read only after the run.
fails_on: B consuming before its phase (completed count != 0)
delivery to a parked B not reaching accepted
either transfer ack other than delivered, or wrong recipient order
a repeated consume (b_again) or the self-transfer consume (a_consume) reporting an unavailable code
a release reporting unavailable when its consume returned non -1, or available when it returned -1
custody not erased, or more or fewer than one custody record
a visit ending in a non-completed reason, or cancellation
tests.unsupported_claim: That custody was erased AT the token's last declared transfer (as the comment says). The test only checks the erased flag at the end of the run, so it cannot show when erasure happened, nor that it did not happen earlier or later. Also unsupported: that consume succeeded in the kernel sense, since native result is not required to be non -1.

tests.asserted: apparatus_complete runs on every capture (principal, calibration, four contrasts) and asserts: envelope passes validate and check_record; execution_form is 'actors'; worker exit witnessed; actor set matches the spec; three-ish distinct PIDs; equipment requested==resolved, requirements satisfied, execution matched, eligible and pid-bound, binding packaged and inventory_verified; each subprocess reaped with exit 0 and parent is the runner; policy actors applied exactly once with the expected sha256 matching the received hash, and the unentitled A is 'unapplied' with count 0; every phase arrival and completion observed with no protocol violations; each step's sandbox check pid matches its actor and comparison order is query_first; every extension event published and attributed to the phase's actor; normalized_outcome is 'finished'. The principal run also asserts B-issue is bound to token 'tb', C's consume to delivery 'dc', the issuer of the second token is actor B, successful reads have the prepared target's inode, and the target file is unchanged. Calibration asserts A's issue returned non-null, transfer delivered and equal, B's consume returned and not -1, B's read failed before and succeeded with matching bytes after (hard failure if issuance is refused). Contrasts omit_b_consume and omit_c_consume assert the chain is incomplete and not credited.
tests.recorded_only: Whether re-delegation is 'credited' in the principal run (usable/first_break) is computed and written to report.json and printed, not asserted: a principal run where the kernel refuses B's second issue or C's read still passes and prints 'not credited; first break at ...'. All per-link kernel outcomes (NULL issue, failed consume, denied read, errno) are recorded. Contrasts remove_b_issuance_allowance and omit_c_extension_predicate assert only the apparatus; their outcomes are recorded with a 'comparison' note, not checked, and 'credited' is just stored. Control-file reads are recorded, not asserted. Only the calibration (and the two omit contrasts) force specific kernel-side results.
fails_on: an actor not being a fresh distinct process, or having wrong policy hash/application count, or A being applied
a missing, unpublished or mis-attributed extension event, or a phase with protocol violations
B's second issue not bound to B's PID or the second delivery not tied to that issue
calibration issuance refused, transfer not delivered/equal, consume failing, or the before-read succeeding / after-read failing
omit_b_consume or omit_c_consume still showing all six links or being credited
an invalid envelope, normalized_outcome other than 'finished', or a modified target file
a duplicate or missing step/event id (by_id requires exactly one match)
tests.unsupported_claim: That the test demonstrates re-delegation works (or fails) on this host. The principal result is only reported; the case passes either way. The two weakened-policy contrasts likewise do not establish that the removed allowance or predicate is necessary, since nothing is asserted about their outcome. Calibration shows only a single A to B hop works, not the two-hop chain.

tests.asserted: Each group is wrapped in check(), so all run and the final assert fails if any failed (failures are also written to assertions.json). Pre-apply run (worker hung before ready, killed by sentinel): files unchanged from seed; envelope validates; every step has comparison observation 'unavailable'/'no_completed_worker_result', order 'unestablished', attempt:not_reached limitation, synthetic sandbox_check with missing_reason validator_not_invoked, attempt missing_reason slot_incomplete, null errno/rc; CLI exit 1, ok false, runner rc 1, test_overrides echoed, worker pid positive and equal to runner pid; ordering shows collection not closed, proceed not set or observed, no worker lifetime, no protocol violations, validator not_invoked; not sandboxed_after_apply, no validator subprocess, partial_steps true, worker term_signal 9 and exit_code None, error mentions pw-probe-runner, attempt outcome 'no_completed_result', prediction outcome is a non-empty string not allow/deny; lifecycle: no ready byte, no done, poll stop 'sentinel_deadline', exit requested, reaped, no wait errors, termination request signal 9 rc 0; no runner_sandbox_denied outcome and no sandbox/policy cause label in diagnostics; normalized_outcome not in the forbidden set (finished, sandbox_apply_failed, bad_policy, runner_sandbox_denied); and no reported apply/compile result fields or prose (library_claims) anywhere. Positive control (same files, policy, plan, no seam): first write changes the file to nonempty different bytes, the denied one is untouched; step 0 allow/succeeded, step 1 deny with EPERM/EACCES permission_failure; outcome 'finished', sandboxed_after_apply true, worker and validator exit 0, distinct pids, sandbox_check rc 0 then 1, validate_step clean. Also asserted (outside check, so they abort main): spawn failure with a bad worker path gives rc 1, 'worker_spawn_failed', posix_spawn in error, no ordering object, no subprocess, files unchanged; and four out-of-range worker args each make the native worker exit 2 with 'out of range' on stderr, and the CLI report runner_failed with exit_code 2, no ready/done, unchanged files, no library claims.
tests.recorded_only: Per-group pass/fail and error strings (assertions.json, stdout). The producer, validator_subprocess and sandbox_check predictions for both runs are saved to prediction_observations.json without being asserted beyond the checks above; the pre-apply prediction's actual outcome string is only required to be a non-empty non-allow/deny string. Before/after file bytes and native stdout/stderr are written as artifacts. The docstring calls the pre-apply gap an 'observed' reporting gap: the test asserts the report must NOT claim a library or sandbox cause, not that any cause is known.
fails_on: the failed-worker report claiming sandbox_apply_failed, bad_policy, runner_sandbox_denied or finished, or including apply_rc/compile_rc fields or 'apply returned/failed' prose
the report attributing termination to the sandbox or policy, or labelling a cause outside CAUSE_LABELS
a file byte changing in the pre-apply run, or the positive control's allowed write not changing or its denied write changing
pre-apply steps reporting a query result or completed attempt, or order other than unestablished
the pre-apply worker not shown as SIGKILLed (term_signal 9) with the sentinel-deadline stop reason
the positive control failing to show allow then deny with EPERM/EACCES, or sandboxed_after_apply not true
argv refusal not exiting with code 2 and the 'out of range' message, or the CLI not reporting runner_failed
tests.unsupported_claim: That the worker failure happened before policy application was observed, or that the policy was or was not compiled/applied. The seam name and the 10s hang are inputs; the test shows only that the reported record makes no completed-result claim and no library/sandbox attribution, and that the policy was not yet shown to be in force (sandboxed_after_apply not true). It also does not show what the worker did or did not start. It is also not an xfail: nothing is excused.

tests.asserted: For each case in the contract fixture (a corpus the test cannot be seen to count beyond the final assertions): exactly one client call; its request contains no 'capture'; no helper inputs; CLI exit code is 0 iff the case is valid, wire result exit_code and ok match; normalized_outcome is 'finished' for valid cases and 'malformed_runner_response' otherwise; the wire runner_result equals what the test's own typed decode of the reply gives (Some or None); data.policy_check is null; diagnostics key is present. Valid: diagnostics is an object and result error null. Invalid but decodable: diagnostics null, reply error null, error text is 'unsupported or malformed compiled_profile' for status_future and 'compiled_profile context is inconsistent' otherwise. Invalid and not decodable: diagnostics null, runner_result null, reply error is a string and equals result error. Finally the admitted labels are exactly ['captured','unavailable'] and the split is (9 refused by admission, 8 by the typed reader).
tests.recorded_only: Nothing is only printed. The fixture contents, and which fields differ per row (nonce, source, params), are not visible and not asserted; the comments say admission ignores them, but the test only observes that the two admitted rows pass and others are refused, not that other fields are ignored in general.
fails_on: a refused receipt admitted, or one of the two valid rows refused (admitted list differs)
a refused receipt reaching exit 0 or outcome 'finished'
the wrong error text for status_future or for the other 8 decodable refusals
a decodable refusal losing its retained decoded runner_result, or an undecodable one having one
a valid case showing null diagnostics or a non-null error, or any case calling the helper or sending a 'capture' request
the 9/8 split of refusal paths changing (e.g. a row moving between admission and reader refusal)
tests.unsupported_claim: That reply admission looks at status and labels 'and nothing else' (test title). The test cannot show that: the corpus is finite, and a decodable invalid row differing only in other fields is not shown to be admitted. It also does not exercise the real worker or real compile; the reply is supplied. Eight refusals happen in the test's own typed reader, not in production admission, so they say nothing about admission logic.

tests.asserted: With the request file replaced inside the client callback, and in the first run (client result with no reply): exactly one client invocation whose input parsed as JSON equals an independently authored expected value (selector removed, augment text spliced with a newline); every helper input equals the client's input byte for byte, and there is at least one; the envelope's policy_check equals the stub capture built for that input; no actor_policy_checks key; exit code 1, normalized_outcome 'xpc_error', runner_result and runner_sandbox_diagnostics null; the request file on disk holds the replacement after the run (in run_held). Second run with a delivered host reply: client input identical to the first, no helper input, policy_check null, outcome 'finished', exit 0.
tests.recorded_only: Nothing in the test is only recorded. The helper's answer is a stub (capture_for builds an 'ok' record of the input hash). The comment states what is not shown. T5 as given has no test attribute visible, and its helper functions are not tests.
fails_on: the client receiving the replaced file instead of the originally read request (the held request not used)
the helper being fed bytes that differ from the client's, or rereading the file
the augment not spliced as '(version 1) (allow default)\n(deny file-read-data)' or the 'runner' selector not removed from the delivered request
policy_check absent or not matching the capture for that input, or present when a reply was delivered
the helper being called when a host reply exists, or a wrong exit code or outcome in either run
more than one client invocation
tests.unsupported_claim: That the fallback policy compiles, or that the shipped client and the shipped helper handle this input; the test's own comment disclaims both, since client and helper are callbacks and the helper returns a canned 'ok'. It also shows nothing about a replaced file's effect on a real run beyond input identity.

tests.asserted: Before the run: the classifier controls (16 constructed samples) must each give exactly the expected history or exception, else the case fails. During the run: the CLI starts; both helpers register; P and C are in one process group led by P; C's parent is P; helper paths equal the provided helper; the worker is named pw-probe-runner and its identity is stable; P's exit event arrives within 2s of the trigger (else assertion); classify_lifetime must succeed, so the case fails if the registered events cannot settle the history (Unresolved: no CLI exit event, no acknowledged ping or snapshot, no exit after release) or if the sample is invalid (changed identity or group, watch registered after trigger, exit before registration). If the descendant was alive, the sensitivity re-sample after release must classify as exited_after_fixture_release. Cleanup errors raise an AssertionError unless a primary error exists; staging is removed only when helper and worker exits and the CLI close are all known.
tests.recorded_only: Whether the descendant was ALIVE or EXITED before cleanup is recorded and printed with verdict None; neither outcome fails. The reply account (CLI rc, validation errors, outcome 'finished', two steps, worker reaped, exit_code 0, exec lifecycle summary 'completed', child_pid, stdout text, observation basis spawned_child, later step ok) is compared and reduced to favorable/unfavorable judgments in account.json with disagreements counted in the printed line, but a disagreement does not raise. The later file effect (bytes equal b'x' and changed from seed) is likewise a recorded judgment, not an assertion. Process and effect observations are written before the JSON is interpreted. Timing deltas, exit-observed-before-or-after CLI completion, and the unidentified termination cause are recorded.
fails_on: a classifier control returning the wrong history or not refusing an unsettled or foreign sample
the leader P not exiting (no event within 2s) after the release byte
helpers not in one group, or C not a child of P, or the worker not pw-probe-runner
no CLI exit event within 25s, leaving the descendant sample unresolved
a missing ping or PID being treated as an exit, or an identity or group change at the registered PID
a live descendant that does not exit after fixture release
a leaked helper or worker or CLI, or a write failure on cleanup.json
tests.unsupported_claim: That the product reports the exec truthfully, or that the later write worked, merely because the case passed: those comparisons are only recorded as favorable/unfavorable and the checker does not fail on them. Equally unsupported: that the descendant is killed or kept alive by ordinary completion, since either history is accepted and the verdict is explicitly None, and the termination cause is explicitly not identified.
